rationale: Operator ruling via decision rubric 2026-10-31. Problem: AISDLC-1119 put a patch-coverage run back into pre-push after DEC-0056 row 2 had deleted the previous local coverage gate; CLAUDE.md and quality-gate.md still say coverage is CI-only. Ruling: register. The step runs the CI script with the CI threshold file (.ai-sdlc/patch-coverage.yaml) over the touched packages only, so one YAML change moves both checks: one standard enforced early, not a second standard. Break-even is one under-covered PR (a CI run, a re-enter, a developer round and a review round saved). Counter-argument weighed: DEC-0056's reasons (bypassable skip var, duplicate run) still partly hold and the step's first run destroyed the parent checkout on 2026-10-30; rebuttal: that gate was whole-workspace and flaked under concurrent worktrees, this one is scoped, the skip var falls under the never-routine rule, and the incident root cause (leaked GIT_DIR into vitest) is closed by AISDLC-1126 and applies to any hook that runs tests. Amends DEC-0056 row 2. Follow-up (docs lane): fix quality-gate.md 'no local pre-push coverage run and no skip variable' and CLAUDE.md 'Coverage is NOT a local gate' to say CI is the only gate that blocks a merge and the pre-push step is its early copy. Rejected: skip/remove (CI round-trip per under-covered PR), opt-in default-off (executors never see it), pipeline-step relocation (double-runs until a second task lands, for a hazard already fixed).
